1800	Understand, even a person who was such a great tzaddik still expects you to do something
1801	for him here.
1802	Kal vachomer father and mother: when a person comes to a Torah class and learns something new he hadn't learned until today, that new thing
1803	crowns his father and mother with a crown up there.
1804	The very fact that a person sits here in class and listens, hearing is like answering. I speak, people listen, it's the same.
1805	The very fact that you learned something new that you hadn't learned until today, they crown your father there.
1806	And if it is on Shabbat, let's read the next passage.
1807	And behold, after Rav Hamnuna made this Torah novelty,
1808	how much joy upon joy there was for the tzaddikim in Gan Eden.
1809	Through this novelty too, joy upon joy arose for the tzaddikim in Gan Eden.
1810	For the tzaddikim have great joy when the extra soul ascends at the end of Shabbat with the Torah novelties it innovated on Shabbat.
1811	And because of this, he merited through his soul.
1812	Therefore, happy are those whose extra soul of Shabbat testifies about the Torah novelty.
1813	It testifies before the Holy One, blessed is He, at the end of Shabbat about the novelty it innovated in Torah.
1814	That is, at the end of Shabbat, a person's soul goes up above to return the extra soul.
1815	And the extra soul reports what more it received in words of Torah.
1816	And afterwards the soul expounds that novelty in Gan Eden.
1817	Then the Holy One and all His retinue, and all the souls of the tzaddikim who were in Gan Eden, bless the father;
1818	all of them are crowned with that word, with that novelty.
1819	It means that all receive lights called crowns through that novelty. And the messenger from Gan Eden also said to Rabbi
1820	Shimon: I also heard from the holy light: how much honor upon honor and crown upon crown crown
1821	the father of that one, for how much honor upon honor and crown upon crown.
1822	At the hour when the Holy One, blessed is He, says: gather to hear novelties and new teachings of Torah in the name of so-and-so son of so-and-so.
1823	At the time the Holy One, blessed is He, tells His retinue: gather to hear novelties and words of Torah said in the name of so-and-so, son of
1824	so-and-so, the Holy One, blessed is He, then mentions his father's name. Therefore they crown him with a supernal crown. How many kiss
1825	his head: how many tzaddikim kiss the head of the father of the one who innovated, how many tzaddikim
1826	crown him as they descend from the upper Gan Eden.
1827	Happy is the portion of those who engage in Torah on Shabbat day more than on the other days.
1828	Happy is the portion of those who engage in Torah on Shabbat more than on all the other days.
1829	For just as the holiness of Shabbat is greater than that of the other days, so one who engages in Torah on Shabbat has a greater merit than
1830	one who engaged in Torah on the other days.
1831	And when he goes to sleep…
1832	they crown his father and mother there.
1833	The Arizal wrote, and these are his words: "Honor your father" — behold, he connected this mitzvah to Shabbat.
1834	It is written "Remember the Shabbat day," and it is written "Honor your father."
1835	Because one must innovate words of Torah on Shabbat.
1836	When the son innovates words of Torah, the father is crowned with crowns in the World to Come.
1837	And that is why honoring father and mother is tied to Shabbat: whoever wants to honor his father and mother should remember the Shabbat day and innovate words of Torah.
1838	And this is their true honor. End of his words.
1839	The Arizal also wrote, and these are his words: it also alludes to what is written in the Zohar in Parashat Shelach, what we just learned.
1840	When a person innovates words of Torah in this world on Shabbat — "innovates" means any new thing you just learned and had not done until
1841	today.
1842	You didn't know it until today.
1843	They crown his father with many crowns in the World to Come.
1844	And this is "Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it": to innovate words of Torah in it, and through you cause crowns for your father and honor him
1845	in the World to Come; therefore "Honor your father" is connected to it. So we said that Rabbeinu the Pele
1846	Yoetz writes: know that father and mother are waiting for you to do
1847	something for them there, and not a day should pass without your doing something for them.
1848	Rabbeinu the Gaon of Vilna writes: just as the fish in the sea crave and long for every drop
1849	of rain, so too the parents, even if they were tzaddikim and have water,
1850	nevertheless right now they are in a state of wanting your help.
1851	How much nachat do you give when your father asks you for a glass of water and you give it to him?
1852	Your mother asked you for something and you gave it, and it gave them nachat.
1853	That is nothing here in this world.
1854	For the World to Come, it is to save them from the harsh judgments.
1855	And in the World to Come it is also to raise them up.
1856	Therefore it is written in the book Sukkat Shalom, by a disciple of the Gaon of Vilna: even those who are remembered after many
1857	years, to rise up to the limit beyond which there is nothing higher. Your parents have already risen very, very
1858	high, and still they long for a drop of rain from the world of action, like fish
1859	of the sea.
1860	When they open their mouths in longing for every drop of rain that falls into the sea, even though they have a sea of infinity,
1861	they wait for something more from the son.
1862	Another Torah class that you attend, another amen, another Kaddish, another blessing with kavanah, another strengthening.
1863	Rabbeinu the Pele Yoetz writes: the main honor of one who honors him after his death is that all that is in his power
1864	to do, he should do every single day, and not forget.
1865	See what he writes.
1866	Not like many ignorant people, who remember their father and mother only on the yahrzeit, on the anniversary,
1867	when they come to say Kaddish and give a little tzedakah and learn something for them.
1868	Not like those.
1869	Woe to the fathers who wait for such sons to redeem them and raise them from the pit of destruction on the day of the yahrzeit.
1870	What they do hardly adds or subtracts.
1871	You need to be, know that day by day you influence your parents, not only on the
1872	anniversary, not only on those days, but simply day by day, each day's
1873	matter in its day: what am I doing to help them there?
1874	And as a person behaves toward his parents, so they behave toward him there after he departs from the world.
1875	It is brought in the book Yalkut Lekach Tov: Rav Levinstein told that within the year that the Saba of Slobodka passed away
1876	and left the world, the Saba of Slobodka appeared to him, Rabbi Eliezer Finkel appeared to him,
1877	and told him: send me more packages on Motzaei Shabbat. He came to him in a dream and told him: keep sending me more packages
1878	on Motzaei Shabbat, packages of Torah novelties, packages of good deeds, send me more, send, send.
1879	Therefore a person must think: the parents are standing and waiting and crying out, save me, help me, no one
1880	can help me except you.
1881	"Rescue my only one from the power of the dog," no one can help me except you.
1882	You, my son, help me.
1883	And therefore you truly need to make an effort and act. It is written in the book Elef HaMagen: even if he thinks
1884	that his father is a tzaddik, let him exert himself for his soul.
1885	Nevertheless.
1886	Know that they still think about and want every small drop that comes from us.
1887	Every minute that a person stays on in a Torah class, they crown your father
1888	there.
1889	Every avoidance of a transgression, every bit less looking at the phone and all kinds of other things, is for father's honor.
1890	It is for mother's honor.
1891	And it truly is for their honor.
1892	The Chafetz Chaim writes in Ahavat Chesed: let a person picture in his mind if
1893	he himself were
1894	thrown into fire and into some kind of suffering.
1895	How would he want them to take him out of there?
1896	You yourself, if you were there.
1897	Kal vachomer, father and mother who labored with all their strength until they made you a man,
1898	took care of you as a child, diapers, all that, raised you, now they want your
1899	kindness.
1900	Even if he was a tzaddik, after all Rabbi Shimon and also Rabbi Pinchas were tzaddikim, and nevertheless they waited
1901	to receive something.
1902	Why?
1903	We have almost ten reasons.
1904	Why a person, even if he was a tzaddik, must have us go and act and learn and strive
1905	on his behalf, even if he was a tzaddik.
1906	First, "there is no tzaddik on earth who does good [and does not sin]."
1907	None.
1908	Rabbi Chaim Palaggi writes: Rabbeinu the Arizal already revealed to us that even complete tzaddikim are judged exactingly, to a hair's breadth.
1909	…
1910	Rabbi Chaim Vital brings
1911	in the name of the Arizal: once they showed him in a vision a sage from earlier times who was judged in heaven
1912	because once, when he walked on Shabbat, a little dirt entered his shoe and he carried the dirt in his shoe without knowing,
1913	and walked four amot in the public domain.
1914	Heaven was greatly stirred about him.
1915	Of course, there are levels up above, higher and higher and higher and higher and higher.
1916	The more a person is advanced, the more he is examined.
1917	Even for something unintentional, even for this, even for that.
1918	He has to undergo rectifications. His punishment isn't necessarily Gehinnom for dirt getting into his shoes, but his punishment
1919	was that he sat outside the partition for two days; that too is a punishment at their levels.
